nodes.label: Shared Supabase Project stisbfahlhquaqhrifjh
nodes.rationale: One Supabase project, two consumers (mobile + web) that must feel like one product; the mobile repo owns supabase/migrations/, and all edge functions deploy with verify_jwt = true.

nodes.label: RLS as the Actual Security Boundary
nodes.rationale: The anon key is public by design on both clients, so owner-scoped RLS on all tables, revoked client DELETEs, validate_owned_references() triggers, and zero-policy service-role tables are the real boundary; client-side checks are UX only — never propose weakening a policy to ease a web feature.

nodes.label: OAuth Redirect Allowlist (spendflow:// Rewrite Bug)
nodes.rationale: The project's Site URL is the mobile deep link spendflow://, and Supabase silently rewrites any non-allowlisted redirect_to to it — the 'Google login opens the APK' symptom. Fix is dashboard-only: allowlist each exact origin as <origin>/auth/callback (loopback IPs auto-allowed, localhost hostname is not); never wildcard; verified via scripts/verify-oauth-redirect.mjs.

nodes.label: receipts Storage Bucket (private)
nodes.rationale: 4 MiB image allowlist, owner-folder paths {uid}/..., reads via 1-hour signed URLs (download-disposition variant post-audit so no object renders top-level), INSERT blocked while deletion_pending.

nodes.label: avatars Storage Bucket (public)
nodes.rationale: 2 MiB allowlist, owner-folder writes, public SELECT; being public it drove the canvas-re-encode fix (P2-3) and the stored avatar_url prefix validation (P3-2).

nodes.label: pg_cron Nepal Gold Rate Schedules
nodes.rationale: 4 schedules (11:00/11:15/11:30/12:00 NPT) POST to fetch-nepal-gold-rate with the service key from vault.decrypted_secrets; first verified fetch of the day wins (idempotent).
